Dealership SEO is a specialised application of local SEO with several structural differences that generic local SEO misses. Inventory volatility is unique: a dealership website creates and removes 30 to 70 percent of its URLs every month as vehicles arrive and sell, while a typical local business has stable pages. This means VDP (Vehicle Description Page) templating, sold-listing handling rules, and inventory schema work matter in dealership SEO and do not exist in generic local SEO. Sales department vs service department GBP separation is a dealership-specific pattern. If your sales department and service department have different entrances, hours, or phone numbers, they should have separate Google Business Profile listings. Generic local SEO assumes one location equals one GBP. Inventory feed connection to GBP gives the dealership listing live vehicle showcases via supported DMS providers. Most generic local SEO programmes do not address this because there is no inventory to feed. Trust signals are weighted more heavily because automotive purchases are high-value and high-consideration. Review velocity targets are 5 to 15 new Google reviews per location per month with response within 24 hours, and average rating above 4.3 stars matters more than in lower-stakes categories. Marketplace cannibalisation is structural in automotive in a way that few other industries face. AutoTrader, CarGurus, Cars.com (US) or mobile.de, AutoScout24 (DE) dominate non-branded category SERPs, and dealership SEO strategy must address this directly through marketplace profile optimisation and brand-query focus.
